name: Bolt.new
description: Browser-based AI full-stack app builder by StackBlitz. Each project is a browser-based session with its own file tree and chat history, running in a WebContainer (in-browser Node.js VM). No persistent cross-project user memory by default.

identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Account required to save work. Authentication is handled through the parent company StackBlitz: users sign in with GitHub OAuth, Google OAuth, or email+password, and multiple methods can be linked to a single account so they are interchangeable. Bolt and StackBlitz accounts are automatically linked; projects live under the StackBlitz account. The open-source self-hosted variant (bolt.diy) uses no account by default and stores everything device-local (IndexedDB/localStorage), with community requests for added backend auth.
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: Yes, via the paid Teams plan. Teams get a shared workspace where collaborators are invited with one click and all see the same projects, UI, and backend environment. Role-based access control exists (e.g., editors vs. view-only links for stakeholders), admin privileges, granular user provisioning/permissions, and organization-wide project sharing. Admin deploy controls restrict which environments members can ship to. Integration access (GitHub, Netlify, Supabase, Figma) is centrally toggled. Tokens are allotted per member, not pooled. Enterprise collaboration is expanding via a Microsoft Azure / Microsoft 365 partnership. The free/Pro tiers are effectively single-user. [uncertain] Exact concurrency/real-time co-editing semantics within a single project.

workspace_model.workspace_definition: A workspace unit is a 'project'. Each project is a self-contained browser session bundling a file tree (project source plus node_modules), an integrated terminal, a preview, and its own chat history. Projects are largely virtual/cloud-scoped: stored under the user's StackBlitz account in a dedicated 'Bolt' collection rather than mapped 1:1 to a local filesystem path. A project can be connected to a git repo and deployed (Vercel/Netlify/GitHub Pages), but the canonical unit is the account-scoped project, not a directory on disk. The Teams plan adds a shared 'workspace' that is a container of multiple such projects for a team.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Sessions (chat conversations) are bound 1:1 to a project. Each project carries its own chat history; opening a project resumes that project's conversation context. Duplicating a project creates a new copy with an EMPTY chat history (history is not carried over). There is no global cross-project conversation thread. [uncertain] Whether multiple simultaneous active sessions/chats are supported within a single project.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Context is primarily project-level: the file tree, chat history, connected integrations (Supabase DB, deploy targets), and an optional .bolt/ignore file (controls which files Bolt's AI considers, accessible via the StackBlitz IDE) are all scoped to the individual project. Global/account-level settings include a user's default model preference (set once across all projects). Team Templates provide reusable starting points shared across a team's projects. There is no automatic per-user durable memory that carries learned context between projects.
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: .bolt/ignore is the main per-project config file controlling which files/paths the AI excludes from context (analogous to .gitignore for AI). It is edited via the StackBlitz IDE, not the standard Bolt.new chat page. [uncertain] Whether a dedicated instructions/rules file (e.g., AGENTS.md style) with a documented cascade and size cap is officially supported; Teams offer shared 'prompts' and 'package guidance' as a team-level instruction layer, but precedence ordering is not clearly documented.
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Not a research/corpus-grounding product. Context grounding is the project's own file tree plus user-attached images/files in prompts (it supports attaching images and files to prompts). Teams can use Design System Agents that ingest a company's UI components, npm packages, Storybook sites, brand assets, and design specs as a grounding corpus for generation. No notebook/source-set abstraction like NotebookLM.

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Hybrid. Chat history is persisted client-side to the browser's IndexedDB (via a useChatHistory hook in app/lib/persistence/ in the open-source bolt.diy). Project code is persisted server-side under the user's StackBlitz account (StackBlitz is migrating to a new project-code storage format as of ~April 2026, after which 'Open in StackBlitz' is no longer offered for migrated projects). The WebContainer runtime itself is ephemeral in-browser. App-level runtime data generated by built apps lives in browser localStorage and is lost on refresh unless an external DB (Supabase) is wired up. In self-hosted bolt.diy, both projects and API keys are stored entirely in the browser (IndexedDB/localStorage) and lost when browser data is cleared.
persistence_and_history.session_history: Chat history is stored per project (in IndexedDB for the hosted/OSS chat layer). It is browsable in the UI as the project's conversation. History does NOT transfer on project duplication (new copy starts empty); the recommended workaround is to generate a summary before duplicating and upload it into the new project. Deletion requires removing both the chat in Bolt and the associated project in StackBlitz. [uncertain] Exact retention policy and whether full chat history is directly exportable as a portable file.
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Minimal layered memory. There is no automatic cross-project user memory store. The durable layer is per-project chat history plus project files. A lightweight global preference (last-used / default model) persists across projects. User-authored persistent context is approximated via the in-prompt attachments, .bolt/ignore exclusions, and (Teams) shared prompts/package guidance and Team Templates. Ephemeral thread state lives in the active WebContainer session. There is no documented auto-generated long-term 'memory' feature comparable to Windsurf/Claude auto-memory.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: [uncertain] No prominently documented full-text or semantic search across past project chats. History retrieval is effectively per-project (open the project to see its chat). Cross-project recall is manual: summarize-and-upload when duplicating. The OSS bolt.diy stores chats in IndexedDB, which is queryable programmatically but not exposed as a polished cross-project search UI.
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: WebContainer sessions are ephemeral: the in-browser VM and any app runtime/localStorage state are discarded on tab close/refresh unless externalized (Supabase). Saved projects and their chat history persist indefinitely under the StackBlitz account until explicitly deleted (which must be done in both Bolt and StackBlitz). No automatic TTL/expiration on saved projects is documented. [uncertain] Whether inactive projects are ever archived or garbage-collected.

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: WebContainer: a proprietary StackBlitz in-browser micro-VM that runs Node.js entirely client-side ('the server is your browser'). Each project boots its own WebContainer, runs npm install (often <500ms via pre-compressed CDN package layers and HTTP cache), creates project files, and serves a live preview. The whole node_modules tree plus source is packed into a compressed blob streamed into shared memory; compiles/builds run in Web Workers that yield to keep the UI responsive. Isolation is the browser tab/sandbox boundary rather than a server container, so no production backend runs there by default; real backends require external services (Supabase, deploy to Vercel/Netlify). In bolt.diy the AI-generated actions are executed by an ActionRunner (app/lib/runtime/action-runner.ts) per artifact, with file- and folder-level locking in the FilesStore.
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: Project source code + node_modules state is effectively snapshotted as the compressed blob and restored quickly on revisit (HTTP cache copy in hundreds of ms). However, this is coupled to the project's stored files, not an independently saved machine/env image. Runtime state of the built app (in-browser localStorage / in-memory DB) is NOT persisted across sessions unless an external database is connected. [uncertain] Whether installed system packages or env-var state are independently snapshotted apart from project files.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: Limited. Projects can be opened in the full StackBlitz web IDE for code-level editing (gives access to .bolt/ignore) and connected to GitHub for export. The OSS bolt.diy can be self-hosted/run locally. There is no seamless cloud<->local execution handoff that preserves the live session state the way some agent CLIs offer; export is via git/GitHub.
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: Primarily single-session per project: one WebContainer per project tab executing actions sequentially (ActionRunner runs AI actions in order per artifact). No documented coordinator-managed parallel-agent fanout or worktree-style parallelism within a project. Parallelism across projects is just multiple independent project tabs/sessions, each with isolated WebContainer state.
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Primarily the Bolt.new web app (browser). Secondary surfaces: the StackBlitz web IDE (for code editing), GitHub integration (import/export), and one-click deploys to Vercel/Netlify/GitHub Pages. Enterprise reach via Microsoft Azure/365 integration. [uncertain] No first-class CLI, Slack, or GitHub-issue-mention trigger documented for the hosted product.

implementation.implementation_stack: Core runtime: StackBlitz WebContainer (in-browser Node.js micro-VM, WASM-based), browser-native IDE loosely based on VSCode. Package delivery via Bolt's CDN serving pre-compressed dependency layers cached in the browser. Chat history persistence: browser IndexedDB (useChatHistory hook, app/lib/persistence/ in OSS bolt.diy); AI action execution via ActionRunner with FilesStore file/folder locks. Project code storage: StackBlitz cloud account backend (format migrating ~April 2026). Identity: StackBlitz auth (GitHub/Google OAuth, email+password). External data persistence: Supabase. Deploy targets: Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages, Bolt Cloud (Supabase-backed). Supports MCP integration and ~19 LLM providers. [uncertain] Exact server-side database technology StackBlitz uses for project storage.
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: Bolt.new maps a workspace to an account-scoped 'project' object that bundles a file tree + a dedicated chat history, with NO automatic cross-project memory — a clean contrast to Labmate's goal of durable user-level memory. Lessons for Labmate: (1) workspace_id == project_id, with session/conversation history scoped strictly to that workspace_id (mirrors Labmate's MongoDB long-term session docs keyed by workspace). (2) Keep a hard boundary between ephemeral runtime state (Bolt's WebContainer / Labmate's Redis Streams active-session state with TTL) and durable stored artifacts (Bolt's StackBlitz-stored project files / Labmate's MongoDB docs). (3) Bolt's 'empty chat on duplicate, summarize-and-upload to carry context' is an explicit anti-pattern for Labmate to avoid — Labmate should instead offer first-class cross-session/cross-workspace recall rather than manual summary porting. (4) Bolt's per-member (non-pooled) token allotment and Teams shared workspace + role model is a useful template if Labmate adds team isolation. (5) Identity: Bolt requires an account (OAuth/email) to persist; Labmate's Discord connector is the analogous required identity/session entry point, and a stable user_id should key the durable memory store the way StackBlitz account keys projects.
